condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

description.narrative: 1. Number of Projects Developed 2. Number of Interventions on Climate Resilience and Enhanced Action Initiated 3. Number of Interventions/Solutions on Human Wildlife Conflict and Wildlife Crime Developed

comment.narrative:
Activity 1: Human-Wildlife Conflict and Wildlife Crime 1. Upgrade of the ENP northern boundary fence 2. Hyenas satellite collars 3. Early warning locker station in HWC prone area 4. Lion satellite collars 5. Building of predator proof kraals
Activity 2: Climate change and resilience Climate Budget Tagging, to develop the tool to tag climate finance in the national budget
Activity 3: Human Resource and Technical Capacity

Activity 1: Human-Wildlife Conflict and Wildlife Crime This activity was reprogrammed, as a result the following activities were undertaken:
1. The Etosha National Park and the Hardap Game Park were supported to strengthen the park boundaries, subsequently preventing rhinos and antelopes from escaping from these parks. Some areas in these parks have also been used by domesticated livestock (goat, sheep and cattle) to graze inside the park which can result in the spread of bovine diseases.
2. Renovation and reconnection of water troughs in the parks so that waterholes can be shifted from the peripherals of the parks to discourage congregation of high value species and other games around waterholes on the outskirts of the parks which may instigate poaching as an anti-poaching initiative.
Activity 2: Climate change and resilience This activity was carried out under Climate Promise I in 2021. The activity will be scaled-up under CP II in 2023.
Activity 3: Human Resource and Technical Capacity 1. UNDP supported the preparation and participation of the Namibian country delegation to the UNCBD COP 15 which resulted in the national paper towards key interventions at the CBD COP in areas of Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS), Marine and Terrestrial Biodiversity and the Financial Mechanism of the COP.
2. Training of, and dialogue with tertiary education students in environmental-related fields on the three Rio conventions which crystallised a common position resulting in the development of Namibian Youth Position Paper on the CBD.
3. The Namibian College of the Arts (COTA) were supported through an Art Competition and an Exhibition under the Stockholm +50 Consultations project with the aim to raise awareness on climate change mitigation and the human/environment development nexus.
4. Public education and awareness raising exercises undertaken on climate change, land degradation and biodiversity through National Television and local language radios featuring high-ranking UNDP/MEFT officials under the Stockholm +50 Consultations project.
5. UNDP supported Namibias first participation in the “Great Southern Bioblitz”, a four-day effort to record all the living species in a designated area in the global south thought the Namib Research Institute at Gobabeb. This resulted in logging more than 2,300 observations of plants, animals and lichens with identification of over 550 species. The principal aim of the Great Southern Bioblitz is to highlight the phenomenal biodiversity found across the Southern Hemisphere. An additional purpose is to foster public engagement with nature, through the citizen science app, iNaturalist (www.inaturalist.org/).
6. Namibia participated in the Stockholm + 50 consultations in four regions in which 202 (81M, 121F) people reached with the consultations with the focus on climate action, early warning systems, food security. The feedback report for Namibia was consolidated along with other country reports to produce a global report presented at the 27th Conference of Parties (COP 27) under the UNFCCC in Egypt 2022.
7. UNDP supported the Namibian delegation preparations to, and participation in the UNFCCC COP 27 which resulted in the development of strategies on how the Namibian delegation can negotiate for investment funding, and technological transfers through COP 27 in order to meet countrys NDC targets. The UNFCCC COP 27 resulted in Namibia mobilizing about USD 740 million from investments resulting in Green Hydrogen.
